chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatarri narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the food of the People of the Book and their marriage, is it permissible? He said, 'Yes, there was a Jewish woman under the authority of Talha.'

key_terms.طَعَامُ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: Food of the People of the Book

ai.seo_question: Is the food and marriage of the People of the Book permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) affirms the permissibility of consuming the food of the People of the Book and marrying them, grounding the ruling in the precedent of Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, a prominent companion known for his piety. This specific citation serves as a crucial evidentiary link in Shia jurisprudence, validating the practice through the example of a Sahabi rather than solely relying on the general Quranic verse. The reference to Talha highlights the continuity of this ruling from the early Islamic period, reinforcing its acceptance among the companions.
